parameters.content:
## Leads → Courier CSV  (Facebook · TikTok · CRM)

**Setup (one time)**
1. **Read Products Sheet** → feeder.retexia.com sends each customer's products from Supabase (`feeder` schema: Feeder products + their form names + their prices). For the n8n form and manual runs, paste the Products Google Sheet link into `PRODUCTS_SHEET_URL` (shared: *Anyone with the link*). No Google login needed; row 1 = headers.
2. **OpenRouter Chat Model** → create an *OpenRouter* credential (API key from openrouter.ai/keys) → pick a model (any cheap one that supports JSON, e.g. `openai/gpt-4o-mini`).
3. Save & **Activate**. **Upload Lead Files** → copy the **Production URL**.

**Daily use** (same as feeder.retexia.com → Bulk import v2)
Open the form → any of: Facebook `.xls/.csv` files, TikTok `.xlsx/.csv` files, CRM Google Sheet links (one per line) → Submit → one `yyyy_MM_dd(orders).csv` downloads.
Form, panel and the manual CRM run all go through **Collect sources** (it downloads the CRM sheets), so they build exactly the same file.

**Columns — any order, any names, nothing required**
Known names (full_name, Name, Phone number, Mobile, Address, City, Form name, Product, Qty, Price/COD, SKU/item_code, Delivery…, Sinhala/Tamil words too) are read instantly; phone columns are also spotted by their values. If name, phone, address or product is not found, **AI: map columns** works it out once and the answer is remembered for that header layout. Missing columns are left blank and listed as ⚠ warnings — the file is still built.
Price / item_code / delivery / qty from the file win; anything missing comes from the matched product. Only 6 sample rows of an unclear file are sent to OpenRouter.

Only stop: a row names a product that is not in the Products sheet (set `STOP_ON_UNKNOWN_PRODUCT = false` in **Build Courier CSV** to build anyway with blanks).

**How products are found**
Each form/product name is split into words and searched in `product_name`, `product_id` and `aliases`. Half the words must match; best score wins; real ties are refused. If a form isn't matched, add it to that product's `aliases`.

price ← price · item_code ← product_ID_Feeder · delivery ← delivery_fee

**feeder.retexia.com → Bulk import**
Panel posts files to **Panel: Bulk import** with header `X-Retexia-Key` (= `KEY` in **Check panel key** = `FEEDER_N8N_KEY`). TikTok files work there too. **Bulk import v2** sends `facebook` and `tiktok` files and `crm_links` (JSON list of Google Sheet links) in one request; **Collect sources** downloads the sheets, so one courier CSV covers everything.

## CRM import (manual)
Usually done from the form or feeder.retexia.com (paste the links there). To run it here:
1. Share the CRM sheet: *Anyone with the link → Viewer*.
2. Paste its link (open the right tab first) into **CRM: sheet link** (several: one per line).
3. Click **Execute workflow** on **Run CRM import**.
4. Open **CRM: courier CSV** → Output → Binary → **Download**.

Columns can be in any order with any names; nothing is required.

## AI column reader
Runs only when name, phone, address or product can't be found by column name. If OpenRouter fails, the columns found by name are used and a ⚠ warning says so.

parameters.formDescription: Same as feeder.retexia.com → Bulk import v2. Use any of the three (at least one): Facebook lead files (.xls/.csv from Leads Center), TikTok lead files (.xlsx/.csv from TikTok Leads Center), and CRM Google Sheet links (Share → Anyone with the link → Viewer; copy the link with the orders tab open). You get one courier CSV for everything.

values.placeholder: One Google Sheet link per line (view access is enough)

parameters.text:
=You read order / lead spreadsheets for a Sri Lankan cash-on-delivery shop (Facebook lead ads, TikTok lead ads, CRM or order sheets). Every file can be different: columns in any order, any names (English, Sinhala, Tamil, long questions, abbreviations), a title row above the header, or no header at all. No field is required — many files only have some of them.

The goal is a courier file with: name, address, phone 1, phone 2, price, qty, item code, delivery fee — plus the product name so the product can be looked up.

For EACH file below, work out which column holds what. Columns are the numbered keys in "cells" (starting at 0). Rows are numbered from 0.

Reply with ONLY this JSON and nothing else:
{"files":[{"file":"<exact file name>","header_row":<row number of the header row, or -1 if there is no header row>,"name":[<customer name column(s); first name then last name if split>],"phone":[<phone column(s); main number first, then a second / work / WhatsApp number>],"address":[<address column(s) in order: street, town/city, district>],"form_name":[<product / package / instant form / campaign name column(s), best first>],"price":<price or COD amount column, or null>,"qty":<quantity column, or null>,"item_code":<item code / SKU / product code column, or null>,"delivery":<delivery or shipping fee column, or null>,"lead_id":<lead or order id column, or null>,"created_time":<date/time column, or null>,"note":"<short note on anything unclear or missing>"}]}

Rules:
- Only use column numbers that exist in the data; use [] or null when a field isn't in the file.
- Decide from the cell VALUES as well as the headers (Sri Lankan phones look like 07XXXXXXXX, 947XXXXXXXX or +94 7X XXX XXXX; prices look like 1990 or Rs. 2,490; qty is a small whole number).
- Never put the same column in two fields.
- Ignore columns that are not listed above (email, status, notes, ad ids, platform…).
